title: Consuming Web APIs from ASP.NET Core with HttpClient
description: Use HttpClient to consume a Web API from an ASP.NET Core MVC application, covering all CRUD operations, security with API keys, file uploads, and format negotiation.

data.text: What Is HttpClient?

**HttpClient** is the primary class in .NET for sending HTTP requests and receiving HTTP responses from a resource identified by a URI. It lives in the `System.Net.Http` namespace and is the backbone of consuming Web APIs from ASP.NET Core server-side code.

data.title: HttpClient is asynchronous
data.text: All HttpClient methods (GetAsync, PostAsync, PutAsync, DeleteAsync, SendAsync) return Task<T>. Always use async/await when calling them, and make your controller actions return Task<IActionResult>.
HttpClient Key Methods

data.text: Client-Server Architecture

data.caption: The APIConsume MVC app acts as a client calling the APIControllers Web API.
data.definition:
graph LR
    C[APIConsume MVC App] -->|HttpClient GET /api/Reservation| S[APIControllers Web API]
    C -->|HttpClient POST /api/Reservation| S
    C -->|HttpClient PUT /api/Reservation| S
    C -->|HttpClient PATCH /api/Reservation/1| S
    C -->|HttpClient DELETE /api/Reservation/1| S
    S --> E[(Repository / In-Memory Store)]
    S -->|JSON Response| C

data.text: Setting Up the Client Project
Create a new **ASP.NET Core Web App (MVC)** project named `APIConsume`. Keep the Web API project (`APIControllers`) running on its own port. The client project will call the API over HTTP.

data.title: Models/Reservation.cs — Shared model
data.content: A simple model that matches the API's Reservation class.

data.title: Newtonsoft.Json
data.text: Install the Newtonsoft.Json NuGet package in the APIConsume project. It provides JsonConvert.SerializeObject() and JsonConvert.DeserializeObject<T>() for converting between C# objects and JSON.
GET — Read All Reservations

The `HttpClient.GetAsync()` method sends an HTTP GET request. The response content is read as a string, then deserialized into a `List<Reservation>` using `JsonConvert.DeserializeObject<List<Reservation>>()`.

data.title: Controllers/HomeController.cs — Index action (GET all)
data.content: Async action that calls the API and passes the list to the view.

data.text: GET by Id — Read a Single Reservation
Append the reservation id to the URL. Check `response.StatusCode` before deserializing — if the API returns 404, the body will be empty and deserialization will fail.

data.title: Controllers/HomeController.cs — GetReservation actions
data.content: Two actions: a GET to show the form, and a POST to call the API with the entered id.

data.text: POST — Create a New Reservation

To **POST** data, first serialize the C# object to JSON with `JsonConvert.SerializeObject()`, then wrap it in a `StringContent` object that specifies the media type as `application/json`. Pass the `StringContent` as the second argument to `PostAsync()`.

data.title: Controllers/HomeController.cs — AddReservation action
data.content: Serialize the reservation, POST it, and deserialize the API response.

data.text: PUT — Fully Replace a Reservation
The PUT method replaces an entire reservation. Since the API uses `[FromForm]`, wrap each field in a `MultipartFormDataContent` object before sending.

data.title: Controllers/HomeController.cs — UpdateReservation action
data.content: Two actions: GET loads the reservation, POST sends the updated values as form data.

data.text: PATCH — Partially Update a Reservation

PATCH requires a custom `HttpRequestMessage` because `HttpClient` does not have a dedicated `PatchAsync()` method. Set the method to `new HttpMethod("Patch")` and provide a JSON Patch document as `StringContent` with media type `application/json-patch+json`.

data.title: Controllers/HomeController.cs — UpdateReservationPatch action
data.content: Build an HttpRequestMessage with the PATCH method and JSON Patch body.

data.text: DELETE — Remove a Reservation
Use `HttpClient.DeleteAsync()` with the reservation id appended to the URL. After deletion, redirect the user back to the Index page.

data.title: Controllers/HomeController.cs — DeleteReservation action
data.content: POST action that calls the API DELETE endpoint and redirects.

data.text: Securing the API with API Keys

In production, Web APIs should be protected so only authorized clients can write data. A simple approach is to require an **API key** in the HTTP request header. The server validates the key before performing the action.

data.caption: API key authentication: client sends key in header, server validates before processing.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client (APIConsume)
    participant A as Web API (APIControllers)
    C->>A: POST /api/Reservation + Header: Key: Secret@123
    A->>A: Authenticate() checks key against allowed list
    alt Key is valid
        A-->>C: 200 OK + created reservation
    else Key is invalid
        A-->>C: 401 Unauthorized
    end

data.title: Controllers/ReservationController.cs — Authenticate method
data.content: Server-side check for allowed API keys in the request header.

data.title: Controllers/HomeController.cs — POST with API key
data.content: Add the key to DefaultRequestHeaders before calling the API.

data.text: File Upload with IFormFile
To upload a file, inject `IWebHostEnvironment` into the API controller to get the `wwwroot` path. The client reads the uploaded file into a `StreamContent` and wraps it in `MultipartFormDataContent`.

data.title: Controllers/ReservationController.cs — File upload endpoint
data.content: Inject IWebHostEnvironment, then save the uploaded file to wwwroot/Images.

data.title: Controllers/HomeController.cs — Upload file from client
data.content: Read the file stream, add to MultipartFormDataContent, and POST to the API.

data.text: Returning XML Instead of JSON
By default ASP.NET Core returns JSON. To return **XML**, register the XML formatter in `Program.cs` and apply `[Produces("application/xml")]` to the action method.

data.title: Program.cs — Register XML formatter
data.content: Add the XML data contract serializer formatter alongside Newtonsoft.Json.

data.title: Controllers/ReservationController.cs — XML action
data.content: Apply [Produces("application/xml")] to force XML output.

data.text: Web API Accepting XML — [Consumes] Attribute
Some APIs accept XML input. Use the `[Consumes("application/xml")]` attribute to restrict the action to XML requests only. The parameter type is `XElement` from `System.Xml.Linq`.

data.title: Controllers/ReservationController.cs — POST that accepts XML
data.content: Accept XML data, extract element values, and create a reservation.

data.title: Controllers/HomeController.cs — POST XML from client
data.content: Serialize the reservation to XML and POST with Content-Type application/xml.

data.text: Format-Specific Methods with [FormatFilter]

A single action method can serve both JSON and XML responses using the `[FormatFilter]` attribute. Add a `{format}` route token and apply the filter — the client chooses the format by appending `.json` or `.xml` to the URL.

data.title: Controllers/ReservationController.cs — Format-specific action
data.content: One method serving both JSON and XML based on the URL extension.

data.text: Testing Web APIs with PowerShell
PowerShell's `Invoke-RestMethod` cmdlet is a quick way to test API endpoints from the command line. It sends HTTP requests and automatically parses JSON responses.

data.title: PowerShell — GET all reservations
data.content: Run in the Package Manager Console or a PowerShell terminal.
data.code: Invoke-RestMethod https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation -Method GET

data.title: PowerShell — POST a new reservation
data.content: Send JSON body with ConvertTo-Json and set Content-Type.
data.code:
Invoke-RestMethod https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation -Method POST \
    -Body (@{ Id = 0; Name = "Mary"; StartLocation = "Tokyo"; EndLocation = "Abu Dhabi" } | ConvertTo-Json) \
    -ContentType "application/json"

data.title: PowerShell — PUT update
data.content: Send form-urlencoded data for a PUT request.
data.code:
Invoke-RestMethod https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation -Method PUT \
    -Body (@{ Id = 5; Name = "Mary"; StartLocation = "Tokyo"; EndLocation = "Abu Dhabi" }) \
    -ContentType "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"

data.title: PowerShell — PATCH update
data.content: Send a JSON Patch document with the correct media type.
data.code:
Invoke-RestMethod https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation/2 -Method PATCH \
    -Body '[{"op":"replace","path":"Name","value":"Bob"},{"op":"replace","path":"StartLocation","value":"San Francisco"}]' \
    -ContentType "application/json-patch+json"

data.title: PowerShell — DELETE a reservation
data.content: Delete reservation id 3 from the command line.
data.code: Invoke-RestMethod https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation/3 -Method DELETE

data.text: CORS — Cross-Origin Resource Sharing

If your client application runs on a different origin (different port, domain, or protocol) from the Web API, the browser blocks the request unless the API explicitly allows it via **CORS**. Enable CORS in `Program.cs` using the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Cors` package.

data.title: Program.cs — Enable CORS
data.content: Allow all origins during development. In production, specify exact origins.

data.title: Build the APIConsume Client Application
data.description: Create a complete ASP.NET Core MVC client that consumes every endpoint of the Reservation Web API.
steps: Create the APIConsume MVC project targeting .NET 8.0 LTS.
Add the Reservation model and install Newtonsoft.Json.
Implement the Index action with HttpClient.GetAsync to list all reservations.
Implement AddReservation (GET form + POST to API) with StringContent.
Implement GetReservation (GET by id) with status code checking.
Implement UpdateReservation (GET form + PUT with MultipartFormDataContent).
Implement UpdateReservationPatch using HttpRequestMessage for PATCH.
Add AddFile action to upload images using StreamContent and MultipartFormDataContent.
Enable CORS in the API project's Program.cs.
Secure the API's POST action with an API key header and test both valid and invalid keys.
data.expectedOutcome: APIConsume can list, create, read, update (PUT and PATCH), and delete reservations through the API. File uploads appear in the API's wwwroot/Images folder. Invalid API keys return a 401 message in the view.

items.text: Newtonsoft.Json is installed in the APIConsume project.
Index action uses HttpClient.GetAsync and deserializes to List<Reservation>.
AddReservation uses StringContent with application/json media type.
UpdateReservation uses MultipartFormDataContent for the PUT call.
UpdateReservationPatch uses HttpRequestMessage with new HttpMethod("Patch").
CORS is enabled in the API project's Program.cs.
API POST action validates the Key header and returns 401 on failure.

items.question: Why does HttpClient need a using block?
items.answer: HttpClient implements IDisposable. Wrapping it in a using block ensures the underlying HttpMessageHandler is disposed after each request, preventing socket exhaustion in long-running applications.

items.question: Why use StringContent vs plain string for the body?
items.answer: StringContent wraps the string and lets you specify the encoding and media type (e.g. application/json). Without it, the server cannot determine how to parse the request body.

items.question: Why no direct PatchAsync() method?
items.answer: HttpClient's built-in methods only cover GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE. PATCH is implemented by building a custom HttpRequestMessage with Method = new HttpMethod("Patch") and sending it via SendAsync().

items.question: When should I use [FromBody] vs [FromForm]?
items.answer: Use [FromBody] when sending JSON in the request body (most common). Use [FromForm] when sending multipart/form-data — typically for file uploads or when the client cannot send JSON.

items.question: Is API key security enough for production?
items.answer: No. API keys are a basic measure. In production use JWT Bearer tokens, OAuth 2.0, or ASP.NET Core Identity for robust authentication and authorization.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: HttpClient is the .NET class for making HTTP calls; all its main methods are asynchronous.
Serialize objects with JsonConvert.SerializeObject() and wrap in StringContent for POST/PUT JSON bodies.
Use MultipartFormDataContent with StreamContent for file uploads.
PATCH requires a custom HttpRequestMessage because HttpClient has no PatchAsync().
Always check response.StatusCode before deserializing to avoid errors on failed requests.
CORS must be enabled on the API when the client runs on a different origin.
API keys in request headers provide basic protection but should be replaced with JWT/OAuth in production.
data.takeaway: You can now build a complete ASP.NET Core client application that consumes every endpoint of a Web API, handles errors, uploads files, and respects security requirements.
